C. COMMIT-FAILURE SELF-HEAL (~127 LOC) — `_REGENERABLE_PREFIX`, `_recover_from_unmerged`, `_INVALID_OBJECT_MARKERS`, `_is_invalid_object_error`, `_staged_index_paths`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`.

comments.body:
Patchset 1 got `Verified -1`; rebuilt the split on a newer base rather than rechecking blind.

**Triage of the -1.** Single failing job (macOS shard; ubuntu shards passed), single failing test: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_inbound_removal_confirmation_a4bd.py::test_pass_summary_reports_the_decline_count` — a reconciler log-capture assertion in a file this change does not touch. Mechanism read off the CI log: the per-link decline is `logger.warning` and DID appear in the captured records; the pass summary the assertion looks for is `logger.info` and did not. `caplog.at_level(logging.INFO)` raises the ROOT level, so a concurrent xdist worker leaving an above-INFO level on the reconciler logger filters the INFO summary while the WARNING still lands. Capture artifact, not behavior.

This is already filed: bug `fanatical-skittish-stud` (355b-11d4-e62c-4eb4), "Log-capture flake in decline-count test under xdist". Sibling change `unheedful-custodial-bluebottle` hit the identical failure in a file it likewise did not touch. Locally the same CI invocation passed 12646 tests on the patchset-1 tree, and the test passes standalone on repeated runs.

**Why patchset 2 rather than a bare recheck.** `unheedful-custodial-bluebottle` (change 1713, "Retry write-side git temp-file faults") merged as c8a380e24c AFTER my base, and it rewrote the very region I was extracting: it deleted `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`, `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S`, `_is_transient_add_error` (now an alias of `gitutil._is_transient_object_write_error`) and `_with_transient_add_retry` from `event_append`, moving the family into the shared `gitutil` seam and renaming `_with_transient_head_retry` -> `_with_transient_fault_retry`. Rebasing conflicted, so I discarded my extraction and re-derived it from scratch against the new `origin/main` (@6f37d9495b) instead of hand-resolving.

Re-measured on that base: `event_append.py` is **743** LOC — 1713 shaved 51, still only 57 under the cap, so the split remains warranted.

Rebuilt result: `event_append.py` **524**, `event_prepare.py` **145**, `event_commit_git.py` **183**. Concern boundaries unchanged; the git-verb module is smaller because the retry family now lives in `gitutil`, which it imports. Re-export list updated to match the new reality — `_with_transient_add_retry`, `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS` and `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S` no longer exist and are gone from it; `_is_transient_add_error` and `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS` moved to `event_commit_git` and are re-exported; `_with_transient_fault_retry` is retained in `event_append` for the self-heal. `gitutil.py` NOT touched.

Re-verified on the new base: all five moved regions byte-identical; both new modules leaf by AST import check; no `src/rebar` file over 800; alias-aware binding completeness clean (aliases `_ea`, `_store_append`, `_store_event_append`; 21 refs; only prose false positives `NAME`/`py`/`write_lock`, none of which exist on `origin/main`'s module either); `make lint`, `make typecheck` (525 files), all 12 runnable `check_*.py` gates, complexity baseline (`new=0 increased=0`), four generators no-diff. Same `Change-Id` preserved so this is patchset 2 of change 1715, not a new change. Full suite re-running before push.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` is **794 LOC** on `origin/main` @5f4a5c1d40 — 6 under the 800 hard cap the CI module-size gate enforces, one feature from breaking the build. Re-measured after the `staging.py` extraction (267 LOC, owner of the `.tmp-newticket` convention) and the compaction change landed; neither relieved the pressure. Flagged by audit ae1b.

It mixes four independent concerns (full call-graph map in a comment):
- **A. pre-lock event preparation** — validate the event dict, serialise CANONICAL bytes, hand to `staging.stage_event`. No lock, no git.
- **B. bounded/retry-composed git verbs** — every lock-held git child, wall-clock-bounded, composing gitutil's index.lock + HEAD-parse retries with a local object-DB retry.
- **C. commit-failure self-heal** — recover a commit git refused for an unmerged (UU) or poisoned (missing-object) index.
- **D. locked write orchestration** — three `lock.write_lock(…, retries=…)` transactions, batch rollback, push/enrich hand-off.

## Approach — extract A and B as leaves, keep C with D
Behavior-preserving: moved regions stay byte-identical apart from import rebinding, and every relocated name is re-exported from `event_append`, so no consumer, monkeypatch target, or import path changes.

1. **NEW `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py`** (A, ~140 LOC) — `EVENT_TYPES`, `StoreError`, `event_filename`, `_ensure_initialized`, `_validate_event`, `_prepare_event`, plus the `canonical_bytes` and `reducer._version` (`KEY_ADD`/`KEY_REVOKE`/`TAG_DELTA`) imports. Composes with `staging.py` rather than duplicating it: `_prepare_event` keeps delegating the `.tmp-newticket` atomic-publish convention to `staging.stage_event`, its docstring pointing at `staging.py` instead of restating it. Leaf: imports `staging`+`canonical` only.
2. **NEW `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py`** (B, ~220 LOC) — `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_run_git`, `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS`, `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`, `_GIT_ADD_BACKOFF_S`, `_is_transient_add_error`, `_with_transient_add_retry`, and the verbs `_git_add`/`_git_commit`/`_git_rm`/`_git_commit_paths`/`_restore_paths`/`_unstage`. Owns `import subprocess`/`import time` and the `# raw-git-ok:` markers, which travel with their functions. Leaf: it **imports** gitutil's shared retries and does **not** edit `gitutil.py` (concurrent work).
3. **`event_append.py` retains C+D** (~500 LOC, ~300 of cap headroom) — `delete_events`, `stage_and_commit`, `batch_stage_and_commit`, `write_and_push`, `batch_write_and_push`, `_rollback_batch`, `_maybe_enrich_drain`, `_silent_unlink`, and the self-heal set (`_recover_from_unmerged`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`, `_is_invalid_object_error`, `_staged_index_paths`, `_REGENERABLE_PREFIX`, `_INVALID_OBJECT_MARKERS`). Docstring retitled to that concern, pointing at the leaves.

### Why C is NOT split out — a deliberate seam choice
`_recover_from_invalid_object` and `_recover_from_unmerged` each re-issue `_git_add`, and `test_event_append_transient_retry.py::test_own_vanished_object_is_regenerated` does a SINGLE `monkeypatch.setattr(event_append, "_git_add", …)` that today reaches BOTH `stage_and_commit`'s add and the recovery re-add through one module global. Moving C out would put those callers in different namespaces and silently decouple that seam. C is also intrinsic to the commit step it heals, so keeping it with D leaves a coherent concern, not a residue. A and B have no such coupling.

## Re-export shim (zero test/consumer edits)
Every consumer and test reaches these symbols through the `event_append` module object. The inventory is derived over all three access forms — dotted `event_append.NAME`, string-literal `setattr`/`getattr(event_append, "NAME")`, **and ALIASED `<alias>.NAME`**, since three consumers import under an alias: `_seam.py` (`_store_append`), `inbound_translate.py` (`_store_event_append`), `tests/scripts/graph/conftest.py` (`_ea`). Aliases are resolved by grepping `from rebar._store import event_append as <alias>` then each `<alias>.NAME`, cross-checked with Serena `find_referencing_symbols`. That found one **alias-only** binding a literal-name grep misses — `conftest.py` calls `_ea.canonical_bytes` — so `canonical_bytes` MUST stay on the namespace. `event_append.py` re-exports, under `# noqa: F401`:

- from `event_prepare`: `EVENT_TYPES`, `StoreError`, `event_filename`, `canonical_bytes`, `_ensure_initialized`, `_validate_event`, `_prepare_event`
- from `event_commit_git`: `_run_git`, `_git_add`, `_git_commit`, `_git_rm`, `_git_commit_paths`, `_restore_paths`, `_unstage`, `_is_transient_add_error`, `_with_transient_add_retry`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_GIT_ADD_ATTEMPTS`
- RETAINED, not moved — concern C calls these directly, so `event_append.py` keeps its own gitutil imports `_with_transient_head_retry`, `discard_unmerged_paths`, `path_is_foreign_to_branch` and the `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S` re-export, plus `_lock`, `LockTimeout`, `RebaseGuard` and `import subprocess` under `# noqa: F401` (tests patch `event_append.subprocess.run`; it is the SAME cached module object `event_commit_git` calls, so that seam still reaches the relocated verbs).

`event_append` calls the relocated verbs by **bare name** (never `event_commit_git._git_add`) so the module-global lookup stays monkeypatch-visible — that preserves the single-`setattr`-reaches-both-callers property above.

## Structural gates checked
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has no `event_append` keys → no path-key churn. `check_raw_git_writes.py` sanctions by inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker, no allowlist → markers travel with their functions.
- `test_lock_retry_zebrafish.py::test_opted_in_sites_are_exactly_the_declared_set` pins `{"event_append.py": 3, …}`; all three `write_lock(retries=…)` sites are in D and stay put, so the count holds.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` — MODIFY: remove concerns A and B, add the re-export shim, retitle the docstring.
- `src/rebar/_store/event_prepare.py` — NEW (concern A).
- `src/rebar/_store/event_commit_git.py` — NEW (concern B).
No test, consumer, or `gitutil.py` change.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] `wc -l src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` ≤ 560 (from 794; ≥ 240 LOC of cap headroom); every `src/rebar/_store/` file ≤ 800.
- [x] `event_prepare.py` and `event_commit_git.py` are each ≥ 100 and ≤ 500 LOC and each a LEAF — neither imports `event_append` nor the other (asserted by both module names being absent from their source), with `import rebar._store.event_append` succeeding.
- [x] Every prior binding resolves unchanged through the `event_append` namespace: `getattr` succeeds on the imported module for each of `stage_and_commit`, `batch_stage_and_commit`, `write_and_push`, `batch_write_and_push`, `delete_events`, `StoreError`, `EVENT_TYPES`, `event_filename`, `subprocess`, `_run_git`, `_git_add`, `_git_commit`, `_git_rm`, `_git_commit_paths`, `_unstage`, `canonical_bytes`, `_GIT_TIMEOUT`, `_is_transient_add_error`, `_INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S`, `_maybe_enrich_drain`, `_recover_from_invalid_object`, `_prepare_event`, `_lock`, `LockTimeout`, `RebaseGuard`.
- [x] Re-export completeness is a CHECKED, ALIAS-AWARE invariant: build the reference set over `tests/`+`src/` as the union of (a) `event_append.NAME`, (b) `(set|get)attr(…event_append, "NAME")`, (c) `<alias>.NAME` for EVERY alias found by grepping `from rebar._store import event_append as (\w+)` — today `_store_append`, `_store_event_append`, `_ea` — then assert `getattr` succeeds on the imported module for every name in it. It MUST fail if `canonical_bytes` is dropped (the alias-only regression this AC exists to catch); a literal-name-only regex is NOT acceptable.
- [x] Default suite (`pytest -m "not integration and not external"`) green with **NO edit under `tests/`**, proven by `git diff --name-only origin/main…HEAD` listing only the three `src/rebar/_store/` paths; `make lint`, `make typecheck`, the `scripts/check_*.py` gates and generators-no-diff all clean.
